subject: Billing simulation + batch/cache playbook for MAP
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@novuscare.com>, Billing Ops <billingops@novuscare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Billing simulation + batch/cache playbook for MAP

Hi Sara / Billing team —

Following up on the mutual action plan (MAP) items we agreed to on Friday. We spun up a quick billing simulation to validate the units-per-dollar under a few realistic traffic shapes and caching/batching assumptions. To be useful for procurement and your FinOps review, we need a couple of inputs from your side (attached is a template csv for traffic slices).

Quick context: our goal is to produce a 3-scenario billing simulation (conservative / expected / optimistic) that shows tokens-per-dollar and per-1k-req cost under three runtimes: hosted (default), dedicated (reserved), and cached-prefetch (aggressive prefix caching + batching). Key knobs we intend to surface:
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + expected generation)
- Cache hit rate for repeated prompts (prefix KV caching)
- Typical batch size (requests batched before GPU step) and max batching latency budget
- p95 latency SLA target and acceptable tails for batching

Action items we need from you:
1) Fill novus_sim_inputs.csv with a small sample of hourly QPS for a week (we only need representative slices, not PII) — column headers in the CSV.
2) Confirm your procurement target for per-request cost (e.g., list price target or target effective tokens/$).
3) Tell us the maximum acceptable p95 latency for user-facing flows (so we can limit batching).

I've attached the CSV template and an initial playbook doc (redwood_batch_cache_playbook_v1.docx) that explains the modeling assumptions. Karthik and Monica — I added preliminary notes in the playbook on sensitivity tests we should run (cache hit rates 0/30/60%, batching 1/4/8/16).

Propose a short call Thursday to walk the assumptions live and agree on the MAP gating for close.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi | Head of Applied Inference 
Redwood Inference

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the template. Attaching a quick exported hourly QPS slice (anonymized) — I dropped it into the template and also included a note about our peak windows. A few clarifying items:
- Our target effective tokens/$ goal is roughly $0.30 per 1k tokens for this pilot (subject to procurement), but we can be flexible if the performance/latency tradeoffs are clear.
- p95 latency target for the patient-facing flows is 350ms; internal async flows can tolerate up to 1.2s.

We can do a 30-min sync Thursday at 17:00 EST if that works.

—Sara

NovusCare

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara@novuscare.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 09:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Billing simulation + batch/cache playbook for MAP

Irene / team —

Pulled Sara's filled inputs and ran an initial sensitivity pass overnight. Key highlights (TL;DR attached as sim_results_summary.pdf):

- Baseline (no caching, batch size = 1): ~ $0.55 per 1k tokens (hosted) for their traffic mix.
- Moderate caching (cache hit = 30%), batch size = 4: cost drops to ~$0.28 per 1k tokens (hosted); p95 increases by ~100ms depending on batching timeout.
- Aggressive caching (hit = 60%), batch size = 8: cost drops to ~$0.17 per 1k tokens on hosted; dedicated pricing reduces compute cost further when sustained QPS>200 req/s.

Important trade-offs and open items:
- Latency: to hit 350ms p95 for patient-facing flows, batching must be bounded (batch timeouts <= 60ms) or we need prefix-cache lookups to serve a large fraction from memory. We should validate expected user prompt repeat rate to justify caching assumptions.
- Cold-starts: dedicated pools reduce variance but require a 3-month commit to be cost-competitive.
- Billing model: our per-token definition must include prompt + generated tokens; procurement typically wants a predictable per-session charge — we should prepare an example invoice line-item.

Suggested next steps (for Thursday call):
1) Walk through the PDF summary and the three scenarios.
2) Agree on p95 guardrails per user flow so we can pin batching thresholds.
3) Decide whether to model a dedicated-reserve option in the MAP (helps NovusCare if QPS sustains).

Attachments: sim_results_summary.pdf (application/pdf), sim_results_details.zip (csvs)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@novuscare.com>, Billing Ops <billingops@novuscare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Billing simulation + batch/cache playbook for MAP

Thanks Karthik — great summary. I've updated the MAP document in Drive with explicit gating language so procurement can sign off:

MAP section (excerpt):
- Economics gating: close contingent on a verified scenario where effective tokens/$ <= $0.30 and patient-facing p95 <= 350ms under expected load.
- Technical gating: prefix caching must show >=30% hit rate in a short preflight (2-day A/B) or we fallback to smaller batch sizes to meet latency.
- Commercial gating: if sustained QPS > 200 req/s, Redwood will propose a dedicated-reserved pricing schedule with a 3-mo minimum commit; otherwise hosted pricing applies.

Deliverables & owners:
- Simulation full report (Redwood, Karthik) — due EOD Thursday after the sync.
- MAP updated doc for legal/procurement (Irene) — draft by Friday EOD.
- Procurement targets + approval to proceed to SOW (NovusCare) — tentative by next Wed.

Call confirmed: Thu 20 Nov 2025 17:00 EST (Zoom link in Drive doc). Please bring any internal latency SLAs or billing constraints.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi | Head of Applied Inference
Redwood Inference
